task_instance: Design the employee-sync path for a multi-tenant BambooHR connector: produce the reference-architecture record (context/container/component views, data flows and trust boundaries, identity/permission matrix, field contract, queue/checkpoint/idempotency model, failure paths, SLOs, retention/deletion, decisions, risks, validation plan), grounded in an existing sample connector.
evidence: Read SKILL.md and its references/official-docs.md (both present next to SKILL.md). The skill is a design-only, documentation deliverable (allowed-tools Read/Glob/Grep/Write/Edit; it explicitly provisions/mutates nothing), so the core deliverable is an architecture record. Created a grounding sample at sample-connector/ (tenants.example.yaml + sync_worker.py + webhooks/receiver.py) representing a naive pre-architecture connector with a shared-admin-key isolation flaw. Used Grep over sample-connector/ to surface the shared-credential/shared-destination isolation risk and missing HMAC/checkpoint/reconciliation. Produced the deliverable at docs/architecture/employee-sync-multitenant.md (158 lines). Verified completeness with a shell keyword sweep: every required Output element is covered (container, component, trust boundaries x2, permission matrix, field contract, idempotency x4, checkpoint x10, failure path, SLO, retention, deletion, decisions, risks, validation plan); the mermaid diagram-as-code fence is balanced (1 opening mermaid fence, 2 total fences = one closed block); and the record cites the grounding sample (2 references to sample-connector). The record separates read vs mutation workers, routes by immutable tenant ID to trusted credential/destination metadata, enforces a field allowlist before queue/storage, models webhook-as-trigger with HMAC + replay rejection, includes reconciliation and rollback, records open approval-gated decisions instead of guessing, and classifies the shared-key/namespace finding as a blocking isolation risk per the skill's Error Handling. No credentials, network, model calls, or MCP/connector tools were used; no files outside the work directory were touched.
